paragraphs.text: Atrial standstill is a cardiac arrhythmia in which P waves are absent on the surface electrocardiogram and the atria cannot be captured by pacing. Fazelifar et al. (2005) noted that atrial standstill is an extremely uncommon arrhythmia that rarely appears to be familial and genetically determined. It has been associated with conditions including congenital heart disease, valvular heart disease, conduction disturbances, Brugada syndrome, myocardial infarction, and amyloidosis.

paragraphs.text: Groenewegen et al. (2003) studied a large family with atrial standstill and screened candidate genes. They identified a novel mutation in the SCN5A gene, asp1275-to-asn (D1275N), in all 3 affected living relatives and in 5 unaffected relatives. The deceased affected relative was an obligate carrier. SCN5A-D1275N channels showed a small depolarizing shift in activation compared with wildtype channels. In the same family, the authors found 2 closely linked polymorphisms in regulatory regions of the gene encoding connexin-40 (Cx40; GJA5), a gap junction protein specific to the atria. The polymorphisms were at nucleotides -44 (G-A) and +71 (A-G). Eight relatives were homozygous for both polymorphisms, a genotype found in only about 7% of control subjects, and 3 of these 8 were affected. In reporter gene analysis, the rare Cx40 genotype gave lower expression than the more common genotype. The 3 living patients were the only relatives who inherited both the rare Cx40 genotype and the SCN5A D1275N mutation. Groenewegen et al. (2003) proposed that each genetic change on its own has a relatively benign functional effect, but that together they eventually progress to total atrial standstill.

paragraphs.text: Makita et al. (2005) identified a novel SCN5A mutation, leu212-to-pro (L212P), in a boy with congenital atrial standstill. His father also carried the mutation but was in normal sinus rhythm, indicating incomplete penetrance. The authors expressed the recombinant L212P channel in a heterologous system and studied it by whole-cell patch clamp. The mutant channel showed a large hyperpolarizing shift in the voltage dependence of activation (-63.5 vs -48.1 mV for wildtype) and of inactivation (-95.6 vs -86.6 mV), and delayed recovery from inactivation. The proband also carried Cx40 (GJA5) polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother; his unaffected father did not carry them. Makita et al. (2005) concluded that genetic defects in SCN5A most likely underlie atrial standstill. They suggested that coinheritance of Cx40 polymorphisms may be a genetic factor that modifies the clinical expression of SCN5A-related atrial standstill.

checks.claim: Homozygosity for both GJA5 polymorphisms +71A-G and -44G-A was found in only about 7% of control subjects.
checks.evidence_quote: which occurred in only approximately 7% of control subjects

checks.claim: Three of the 8 relatives homozygous for the GJA5 +71A-G and -44G-A polymorphisms had atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: and three of these relatives were affected by AS

checks.claim: The 3 relatives with atrial standstill who were homozygous for the GJA5 polymorphisms also carried the SCN5A D1275N mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: The three living AS patients exclusively coinherited both the rare Cx40 genotype and the SCN5A-D1275N mutation.

checks.claim: In reporter gene analysis, the rare GJA5 genotype gave lower expression than the common genotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Rare Cx40 genotype reporter gene analysis showed a reduction in reporter gene expression compared with the more common Cx40 genotype.

paragraphs.text: Makita et al. (2005) identified a leu212-to-pro (L212P) mutation in the SCN5A gene in an 11-year-old boy with congenital atrial standstill. His father also carried the mutation but was in normal sinus rhythm. In whole-cell patch clamp studies, the recombinant channel showed a large hyperpolarizing shift in the voltage dependence of activation (-63.5 vs -48.1 mV for wildtype) and of inactivation (-95.6 vs -86.6 mV), and delayed recovery from inactivation. The proband also carried connexin-40 (GJA5) polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother. The authors suggested that these polymorphisms modify the clinical expression of the SCN5A mutation.

checks.claim: Makita et al. (2005) identified a leu212-to-pro (L212P) mutation in the SCN5A gene in an 11-year-old boy with congenital atrial standstill.
checks.evidence_quote: The novel SCN5A mutation L212P was identified in the proband (age 11 years) and his father.

checks.claim: The father of the 11-year-old boy with congenital atrial standstill carried the SCN5A L212P mutation but was in normal sinus rhythm.
checks.evidence_quote: The novel SCN5A mutation L212P was identified in the proband (age 11 years) and his father. The father was in normal sinus rhythm.

checks.claim: In whole-cell patch clamp studies, the recombinant SCN5A L212P channel showed a large hyperpolarizing shift in the voltage dependence of activation (-63.5 mV vs -48.1 mV for wildtype).
checks.evidence_quote: large hyperpolarizing shift in both the voltage dependence of activation (WT: -48.1 +/- 0.9 mV; L212P: -63.5 +/- 1.5 mV; P < .001)

checks.claim: In whole-cell patch clamp studies, the recombinant SCN5A L212P channel showed a hyperpolarizing shift in the voltage dependence of inactivation (-95.6 mV vs -86.6 mV for wildtype).
checks.evidence_quote: and inactivation (WT: -86.6 +/- 0.9 mV; L212P: -95.6 +/- 0.8 mV; P < .001)

checks.claim: In whole-cell patch clamp studies, the recombinant SCN5A L212P channel showed delayed recovery from inactivation.
checks.evidence_quote: and delayed recovery from inactivation.

checks.claim: The proband with the SCN5A L212P mutation also carried connexin-40 (GJA5) polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother.
checks.evidence_quote: the proband, but not his father, carries Cx40 polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother.

checks.claim: Makita et al. (2005) suggested that connexin-40 (GJA5) polymorphisms modify the clinical expression of the SCN5A L212P mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Coinheritance of Cx40 polymorphisms is a possible genetic factor that modifies the clinical manifestation of this inherited arrhythmia.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly; 'possible' is hedged slightly more than the draft.
